title: Crypto OTC Desk Software: What an Auditable Off-Exchange Workflow Looks Like
content_html:
Large crypto trades still get matched in Telegram chats. Two parties agree on a price in a group message, transfer on trust, and keep a screenshot as the record. That holds up until a counterparty disputes a fill, a settlement quietly fails, or an auditor asks for records that do not exist.

What crypto OTC desk software has to cover

An OTC desk matches large orders off-exchange, away from public order books, so a block trade does not move the market price against the trader. Software that runs this workflow needs four things:

1. Order matching off the public books. The order is visible to selected counterparties, not to the whole market.
2. Counterparty whitelisting. Only approved parties can see or fill an order.
3. A defined settlement window. Both sides know when the trade must settle, instead of an open-ended wait for a wire to clear.
4. Automated confirmation records. Each step produces a record at the moment it happens, not a write-up after the fact.

A desk run over chat gets the first item and none of the others.

How Cryptool's OTC desk module handles it

Cryptool's OTC desk module matches large orders off-exchange with configurable settlement windows, counterparty whitelisting, and automated confirmation records. It is aimed at operators who need an auditable OTC workflow without building one internally.

A typical flow: an operator lists a block order on the desk. Only whitelisted counterparties can see it. When a counterparty accepts, the trade gets its settlement window, and both sides receive confirmation records that can be exported for compliance.

The platform is non-custodial, so assets stay in the parties' own wallets. The OTC desk sits in the same platform as Cryptool's Portfolio, Raise, Invest, and Fund Admin modules, which means the resulting position shows up in the same dashboard that tracks the rest of the portfolio. On-chain modules run on EVM chains and MultiversX today, with more chains rolling out, and the portfolio module tracks wallets on any chain from any provider.

Cryptool has facilitated $10M+ in managed capital across 25+ pools, per internal traction data as of 2026-05-20.

Frequently asked questions

What is crypto OTC desk software?
Software that matches large crypto orders off-exchange, controls which counterparties can participate, sets a settlement window for each trade, and records every step so the desk can pass an audit.

Does Cryptool hold funds during an OTC trade?
No. Cryptool is non-custodial. Assets stay in the counterparties' own wallets.

Which chains does the OTC desk support?
On-chain modules run on EVM chains and MultiversX today, with more rolling out. Portfolio tracking works across all chains and all wallet providers.

Who is the OTC desk module for?
Funds, syndicates, and treasury operators whose order sizes are large enough to move prices on a public exchange, and anyone who needs settlement records rather than chat screenshots.
